doc.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021

title: Sources of inspiration and programmatic music
summary: Blake lists film noir, Monk, singers and composers as inspirations; his music captures him rather than the reverse.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So these days, or throughout your career, can you describe to me where your inspiration to compose can come from?

They come from a sense of life, they come from the street, they come from film noir and to be more precise I think of Thelonious all the time, Abbey Lincoln, Billie Holiday, Al Green, Ray Charles, you can guess what my favorite instrument is. Piano is my third favorite. And I think of Bartok and Olivier Messiaen “Quartet for All Time,” and the palette of Debussy, and that I might switch to Humphrey Bogart, Ethel Barrymore, and Dorothy Dandridge. So these memories come right back to me.
Would you say your music, I’m not sure how to put this, but a number of composers have written what we call programmatic music. They’re trying to capture an event, a setting. Is
your music programmatic in a sense that you were inspired by something and you are trying to capture it in your music? In your piano music?

I think so but sometimes I mean Beethoven was very deliberate on the Pastoral Symphony. I know there’ve been many pieces that describe a character. I think instead of trying to capture it though, it captures me.
